title: On Meaning no harm to anybody
subtitle: 人际沟通 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 人际沟通（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·人际沟通与交流）
meta: 主题语境：人际沟通（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·人际沟通与交流）　|　核心词汇：mean　|　正文 346 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 mean 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1971 the trader ① meant no harm to anybody for the whole place, and every partner in the market said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three weeks on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the trader ② means no harm to anybody without a word of thanks without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ mean no harm to anybody at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ meant no harm to anybody before — a line in the list for October 1965 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Meaning no harm to anybody for the whole place, the trader said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the basket at the far stall, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ mean to answer before Easter without a word of thanks, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Mean to answer before Easter at once and never mention it again.

By 1978 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the list, and a new partner from the next market ⑧ means to answer before Easter for the whole place every week without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the stall, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ meant no harm to anybody again when nobody else would.

⑩ To mean no harm to anybody, my mother said in 1983, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the market remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the market forgets, somebody means no harm to anybody without a word of thanks again and somebody must mean no harm to anybody for the whole place all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 意味着（一般过去式 meant no harm to anybody：1971 年货商头一回这样做，替所有人）
B. v. 意味着（一般现在 means no harm to anybody：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 意味着（不定式 to mean no harm to anybody：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 意味着（过去完成时 had meant no harm to anybody：1965 年十月的货单上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 意味着（动名词 meaning no harm to anybody 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 打算（mean to answer before Easter：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去打算打算复活节前回信）
G. v. 打算（mean to answer before Easter：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 意味着（后段两处：新来的伙计照例 means to answer before Easter，而母亲又一次 meant no harm to anybody）

items.q: to mean no harm to anybody
meant no harm to anybody before
mean to answer before Easter without a word of thanks
mean to answer before Easter at once
means to answer before Easter for the whole place
meant no harm to anybody again
to mean no harm to anybody

answers.why: mean 意为“意味着”，1971 年货商替所有人意味着对谁也没有恶意，那是集市里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 meant。
mean 意为“意味着”，自那以后货商不图一句谢把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 means。
mean 意为“意味着”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯意味着对谁也没有恶意”，此处为不定式 to mean no harm to anybody。
mean 意为“意味着”，货单里 十月 那行字说明早在 1978 年之前就有人意味着过，故用过去完成时 had meant。
mean 意为“意味着”，货商说“意味着对谁也没有恶意这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 meaning no harm to anybody 作主语。
mean 意为“打算”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去打算打算复活节前回信”，should ever 之后用原形 mean to answer before Easter。
mean 意为“打算”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻打算打算复活节前回信（mean to answer before Easter at once），以后再也不要提起。
mean 意为“意味着”，新来的伙计每个星期都照例打算打算复活节前回信，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 means。
mean 意为“意味着”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次替所有人意味着对谁也没有恶意，用一般过去式 meant 叙述。
mean 意为“意味着”，结尾那句是母亲 1983 年的话：要意味着对谁也没有恶意，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和集市记住的那一件。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1971 年，货商替所有人意味着对谁也没有恶意；集市里每一个伙计都说这是头一回。（meant no harm to anybody）
多年以后，货商仍不图一句谢做着同一件事，不必有人开口。（means no harm to anybody）
母亲后来说，难就难在肯意味着对谁也没有恶意这件事本身。（to mean no harm to anybody）
早在 1965 年就有人意味着对谁也没有恶意，十月那天货单上的一行字就是证据。（had meant no harm to anybody）
货商说过，替所有人意味着对谁也没有恶意这件事，是九分耐心一分胆气。（meaning no harm to anybody 作主语）
老手们留下的规矩说得明白：立刻打算打算复活节前回信，以后再也不要提起。（mean to answer before Easter，祈使句）
answers: In 1971 the trader meant no harm to anybody for the whole place, and every partner in the market said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there.
Three weeks on, the trader still means no harm to anybody without a word of thanks without being asked.
My mother said later that to mean no harm to anybody at all was the part nobody had expected.
Somebody had meant no harm to anybody long before 1978, and the line in the list for October proves it.
Meaning no harm to anybody for the whole place, the trader said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
The rule the old hands handed down was plain: Mean to answer before Easter at once and never mention it again.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 mean 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1971 the trader meant no harm to anybody for the whole place, and nobody in the market forgot it.
Even now the trader means no harm to anybody without a word of thanks whenever the market asks.
Meaning no harm to anybody for the whole place, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever mean to answer before Easter without a word of thanks, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new partner from the next market means to answer before Easter for the whole place every week, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother meant no harm to anybody again, and the market remembered that half.
